question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2-x}{x+3}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

$$
y = \dfrac{2-x}{x+3}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x = \dfrac{2-y}{y+3}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2-y}{y+3} \\ x(y+3) & =2-y \\ xy+3x & =2-y \\ xy+y & =2-3x \\ y(x+1) & =2-3x \\ y & =\frac{2-3x}{x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2-3x}{x+1}.
$$
